title: FPRC decision Neculau Rom Accepted
text:
FOUL PLAY REVIEW COMMITTEE
DECISION
PARTICULARS OF OFFENCE
Player’s surname Neculau Player’s Vlad
forename(s)
Player’s Union ROMANIA
Match ROMANIA v URUGUAY
Competition November Series 2025 Match Date 22.11.25
SELECT: Red card ☒ Citing ☐
Offence 9.20(b) - Dangerous Clean Out
Finding of Committee
The Player accepts his clean out of the opposing player was reckless, constituted foul
Foul play determined? play, and warranted a red card.
Red card upheld?
The FPRC accepts that this was reckless rather than intentional, but it was an ugly
collision which might, had the circumstances been slightly different, have resulted in
serious injury,
The FPRC is persuaded that there is no reason for this matter to go beyond the
mandatory mid-range entry point of 6 weeks.
The player does not have a clean record, and three previous dismissals means that full
mitigation cannot apply. However, the FPRC does note that the last dismissal was
three years ago, and taking into account the plea, remorse shown and apology given
is prepared to allow mitigation of one third.
The player has not previously undertaken the coaching intervention programme, and
the FPRC is content that this would be an appropriate case for that to be offered.
Summary of Sanction
4 weeks suspension (3 if the coaching intervention programme is opted for)
Matches/tournaments
1. 26.11.25 Timiasora v Dinamo.
included in sanction
2. 6.12.25 Wolves v Lusitanos.
3. 13.12.25 Devils v Wolves.
4. 20.12.25 FInal of the Romanian Cup (if Timiasora qualify) - or - 8.2.26 Germany v
Romania
THE PLAYER WILL BE AVAILABLE FOR NO.4 IN THE EVENT OF SUCCESSFUL
COMPLETION OF THE COACHING INTERVENTION
REASONS FOR DECISION
1. Reckless clear out leading to contact with the head.
2. Contravention of Law 9.20(b) thus demonstrated.
3. Contact with the head means mid-range minimum.
4. Nothing in the case to take it to top range. Hence 6 week starting point.
251125 FPRC Decision Vlad Neculau (Romania) Page 1 of 2

5. Previous dismissals mean full mitigation not available.
6. However, other factors justify mitigation at 33%.
7. 4 match suspension; reduced to 3 if coaching intervention programme utilised and successfully
completed.
R DUNLOP KC, O Tonu’u, J-P Spirandelli
Foul Play Review
Committee Members
